title: Closing the three invisible strict reds: boundary ratchet, 11 runtime gaps, 8 inheritance markers
goal: The previous round zeroed the historical evidence-schema reds and reported three remaining strict red lines as findings G-03/G-04/G-05. This round closes all three by executing what each gate already prescribes, without weakening any checker, adding a baseline entry or re-judging a historical round. G-04 (P2): check-boundaries --root . --strict reported 1 finding, the type-only import of MenuNode from ../system/iam/menu/api in frontend/src/modules/platform/widgets.tsx, frozen in config/boundary-baseline.json since 2026-09-22 with its own ratchet 'promote MenuNode to a shared contract type (frontend/src/api)'. The ratchet was executed: MenuNode now lives in frontend/src/api/menu.ts (the public-contract location named by REPOSITORY_LAYOUT.md §8.1), modules/system/iam/menu/api.ts imports and re-exports it so all seven existing consumers are untouched, widgets.tsx imports the shared type, and the baseline entry was deleted because stale entries fail --strict, leaving entries: [] while the CI --baseline form stays exit 0. G-03 (P3): check-runtime-evidence --root . --strict exited 1 with 0 errors / 11 warnings (this checker treats warnings as blocking); 11 historical commands.json files flagged runtime-sensitive by their task manifest recorded neither a runtimeLogs/Metrics/Traces/Performance signal nor a runtimeGap. Each got one runtimeGap line restating only what its own commands.json and summary.md already say, so the closure is mechanically provable as structure-only: every file is 1 insertion / 0 deletions and no diff line touching "status" exists. G-05 (P3): check-inheritance-contract run from the workspace root reported 8 findings — 3 missing markers in docs/WORKSPACE_INHERITANCE.md, 3 missing markers plus an unpinned Base version in pantheon-ops/docs/PROJECT_INHERITANCE.md, and no .github/pull_request_template.md at the workspace root. All 8 are closed with the literal marker text the checker matches (it is a case-sensitive includes, so 'Generic drift' does not satisfy 'generic drift'), the Base version pinned to the value already recorded in pantheon-ops/foundation-release.lock.json and .business-overlay-report.json, and the same drift markers also added to the template ops actually uses. Root cause is the second occurrence of the FR-016 class — sensors nobody invokes cannot ratchet — recorded as FR-017 with a guide-updated promotion (README invocation forms) and the CI wiring left open for the maintainer.
findings: G-04 (closed): platform -> system/iam/menu type import eliminated by promoting MenuNode to frontend/src/api/menu.ts; check-boundaries bare --strict went from 1 finding / exit 1 to 0 findings / 0 stale / exit 0, and the CI --baseline form stays exit 0 with baselined dropping from 1 to 0. config/boundary-baseline.json now has entries: [] — its last tracked debt was executed, not renewed.

G-03 (closed): 11 historical commands.json files carry a runtimeGap; check-runtime-evidence --root . --strict is 0 errors / 0 warnings / exit 0 (55 evidence sets, including this round own). Two of the 11 (2026-10-07-performance-followup, 2026-10-07-upgrade-runbook) did capture runtime data — P95 1.18s, EXPLAIN, MySQL connection counters, and a disposable v12 -> v21 -> restore rehearsal — but only in their summary.md prose, which is what the runtimeGap strings say instead of inventing structured signals.

G-05 (closed): check-inheritance-contract --root .. --strict is 0 findings / exit 0. Note the workspace root is not a git repository (its .git/ holds only hooks/ and info/ and git rev-parse fails), so the .github/pull_request_template.md the gate requires there can never be auto-loaded by GitHub; the same markers were therefore also added to pantheon-ops/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md so the requirement is not satisfied by an inert file alone.

FR-017 (open, guide-updated): all three checkers were red on main and nothing invoked them — check-runtime-evidence and check-inheritance-contract have no npm script and appear in no workflow, and check-boundaries appears only in ci.yml with --baseline, so its bare --strict reading had never been observed. Registering the class and documenting the invocation forms is what this round could do; promoting them to blocking CI steps is the maintainer's gate-policy decision, same disposition as FR-016.

F-13 (documented risk): pantheon-ops/docs/PROJECT_INHERITANCE.md now states Base version as a second copy of foundation-release.lock.json. Nothing machine-checks that the two agree, so it can drift. Marked in the doc as a must-sync line; a checker comparing them was deliberately not introduced this round.

F-14 (pre-existing, untouched): running gofmt -l . from the pantheon-base repository root lists files under dist/foundation-releases/** (vendored release bundles). From backend/ the tree is clean; this round changed no Go file.

implementationNotes: Only the MenuNode interface moved. MenuPayload, MenuListQuery and the apiRequest calls stay in the menu module: what crosses the layer boundary is the contract type, and promoting the rest would turn implementation shape into public surface.

The baseline entry had to be deleted, not kept: check-boundaries treats an entry that no longer matches a finding as stale and fails --strict on it, which is what stops a removed violation from being silently re-introduced later.

check-inheritance-contract markers are matched with a case-sensitive String.includes, so the first draft's 'Generic drift' / 'Pseudo-drift' bullets still reported missing; the file now uses the exact lowercase strings from REQUIRED_PR_MARKERS.

check-runtime-evidence counts warnings as blocking under --strict, which is why G-03 read as exit 1 with 0 errors. The fix is the schema field (a runtimeGap string), never a runtimeLogs array invented to make the warning disappear.

Backfill was applied by a replayable gitignored script (frontend/.tmp/g03-backfill.mjs) that inserts one line before the top-level knownGaps key and JSON.parse-validates the result before writing, so all 11 edits share one shape and each file stays 1 insertion / 0 deletions.

The integrity proof for this round is narrower than the previous one: git diff filtered to added/removed lines and grepped for "status" is empty. Grepping the whole diff is not, because context lines around an insertion legitimately contain status.
